# Limitations, ethics and responsible use

## What the results can and cannot support

* Every performance number comes from a **synthetic benchmark generated by this project**. It
  shows how the methods respond to the injected signal patterns. It says nothing about how often
  they would find real theft in Karnataka or elsewhere.
* Labels are perfect and immediate. Real labels come from inspections that are sparse, delayed,
  biased toward already-suspected consumers and sometimes wrong.
* Injections are idealised: known start and end, known magnitude, simple shapes. Real tampering
  may be intermittent, adaptive or mixed with legitimate changes.
* The supervised models were trained on the same generator that produced the test data
  (different seeds and runs, same assumptions). Out-of-distribution behaviour is not tested, and
  real deployment would need retraining on real, inspected data.
* The demonstration seed (2043) was *chosen* because it illustrates the mechanisms clearly. It is
  an illustration, not evidence.

## Network and physics

* The topology is illustrative. Only the names "Sharavathi" (generation) and "SRS Peenya"
  (receiving station) are anchored to public sources; no dedicated line between them is claimed.
* Feeders are reduced (2–4 DTs). Each DT's LV network is one equivalent branch; there are no
  phase imbalance, harmonics, voltage-dependent loads or OLTC/capacitor control.
* Losses are computed from hourly-average power. Intra-hour variation would add losses (loss
  factor) that are not modelled.
* Dispatch and the aggregate 66 kV load are stylised.

## Measurement assumptions

* Full smart-meter (AMI) coverage and a meter on every DT are assumed. Many real networks have
  partial DT metering; without DT meters, localisation is only possible to feeder level.
* Meter error is Gaussian bias plus random error. Real faults (CT saturation, wrong multiplying
  factor, clock drift) are not modelled.
* Loss calibration on the reference period removes persistent loss-model bias, but **it would
  also absorb any non-technical loss present during the reference period**. The synthetic history
  is clean by construction, which flatters calibration.

## Known weaknesses found by the experiments

See `docs/experiments/results.md` for the numbers.

* With calibration switched off, a persistent 20–40 % under-estimate of technical losses makes
  the boundary model flag 99–100 % of normal feeder windows (results §6.5). Calibration removes
  this, at the cost described above.
* Higher meter noise than the uncertainty model assumes raises false alarms at boundary level
  (false-positive rate 0.03 → 0.12 at 4× noise): the propagated σ uses nominal accuracy figures,
  so unknown extra noise inflates z-scores.
* Heavy missing data (20 % of readings) raises the boundary model's false-positive rate from 0.03
  to 0.29. The priority scheme routes low-coverage alerts to meter-data review (DQ), but the
  classifier itself does not abstain.
* At feeder level, a default-threshold energy-balance rule is very precise but misses most small
  events; tuned on validation it comes close to the boundary Random Forest (F1 0.838 vs 0.867).
* Isolation Forest got **worse** when grid features were added: as an unsupervised method it
  treats all features alike and is diluted by them.
* Genuine consumption drops remain the main consumer-level false-positive source, especially
  when they occur inside a DT that also has a real gap.
* Small residential under-recording is hard to see at feeder level: a few kWh/day disappear in
  meter and loss-model uncertainty.

## Ethics and safety

* Outputs are **investigation-prioritisation signals**, never accusations or legal findings.
  Anomaly detection, risk ranking and legal determination are kept separate; the software does
  only the first two.
* An unexplained energy imbalance can come from technical losses, meter error, missing or
  delayed data, timing mismatches and outages, not only theft. The UI states this wherever a
  balance is shown.
* Real investigations require authorised field inspection under the utility's procedures and
  the Electricity Act; customers are entitled to due process.
* All identifiers are synthetic. No personal data is processed.
* The software does not connect to, or send commands to, any real grid equipment, SCADA, AMI
  head-end or utility system, and requires no credentials.
* Scenario injections change synthetic numbers only. The project describes no method of
  tampering with meters or bypassing metering.
